Statement following ‘productive’ talks in Washington comes as Israel launches strikes on southern city of Tyre Israel and Lebanon have agreed to a 45-day extension of their ceasefire after another round of talks in Washington, the US state department has said. It came after two “productive” days of talks, and more negotiations would be held from 2-3 June, the department spokesperson Tommy Pigott said. The shaky truce between Israel and the Hezbollah militant group in Lebanon had been due to end on Sunday. Pigott said on social media: “We hope these discussions will advance lasting peace between the two countries, full recognition of each other’s sovereignty and territorial integrity, and establishing genuine security along their shared border.”

Israel and Lebanon have agreed to a 45-day extension of their ceasefire after another round of talks in Washington, the U.S. State Department said Friday. It comes after two "productive" days of talks and will be followed by more negotiations June 2 and 3, State Department spokesperson Tommy Pigott said. A shaky truce between Israel and the Hezbollah militant group in Lebanon had been due to end on Sunday. "We hope these discussions will advance lasting peace between the two countries, full recognition of each other's sovereignty and territorial integrity, and establishing genuine security along their shared border," Pigott said on social media. While a key objective of Friday's talks was extending the tenuous ceasefire between Israel and Hezbollah, both sides continue to trade strikes.

Israel has been pounding Lebanon and invaded its south in response to fire from Hezbollah, the Iranian-backed Shia movement that is not part of the ceasefire diplomacy. Even as talks were wrapping up in Washington, Israel’s military issued evacuation orders for the southern city of Tyre, where it said it was hitting Hezbollah infrastructure. An AFP correspondent reported a series of strikes, two of them near Tyre, while state media said another targeted a centre run by a local NGO near a hospital. The Israeli military said it had struck Hezbollah sites in southern Lebanon after reporting hostile aircraft alerts and launches from across the border. Lebanon’s health ministry said the strikes on the Tyre district wounded at least 37 people, including six hospital personnel, nine women and four children.

Statement following ‘productive’ talks in Washington comes as Israel launches strikes on southern city of Tyre

Israel and Lebanon have agreed to a 45-day extension of their ceasefire after another round of talks in Washington, the US state department has said.

It came after two “productive” days of talks, and more negotiations would be held from 2-3 June, the department spokesperson Tommy Pigott said.

The shaky truce between Israel and the Hezbollah militant group in Lebanon had been due to end on Sunday.

Pigott said on social media: “We hope these discussions will advance lasting peace between the two countries, full recognition of each other’s sovereignty and territorial integrity, and establishing genuine security along their shared border.”

Israel has been pounding Lebanon and invaded its south in response to fire from Hezbollah, the Iranian-backed Shia movement that is not part of the ceasefire diplomacy.

Even as talks were wrapping up in Washington, Israel’s military issued evacuation orders for the southern city of Tyre, where it said it was hitting Hezbollah infrastructure.

An AFP correspondent reported a series of strikes, two of them near Tyre, while state media said another targeted a centre run by a local NGO near a hospital.

The Israeli military said it had struck Hezbollah sites in southern Lebanon after reporting hostile aircraft alerts and launches from across the border.

Lebanon’s health ministry said the strikes on the Tyre district wounded at least 37 people, including six hospital personnel, nine women and four children.

One strike “levelled” a primary healthcare centre and damaged the neighbouring Hiram hospital, wounding six medical staff members, the statement said.

The US steadfastly backs Israel, with which it attacked Iran on 28 February, but has also gently voiced unease about Israeli troops’ control of southern Lebanon.

“We hope these discussions will advance lasting peace between the two countries, full recognition of each other’s sovereignty and territorial integrity, and establishing genuine security along their shared border,” Pigott said.

Israel’s ambassador to Washington, Yechiel Leiter, who led his country’s delegation, said after the talks that it would be critical to ensure Israel’s security.

“There will be ups and downs, but the potential for success is great,” Leiter wrote on X.

Israel and Lebanon have agreed to a 45-day extension of their ceasefire after another round of talks in Washington, the U.S. State Department said Friday.

It comes after two "productive" days of talks and will be followed by more negotiations June 2 and 3, State Department spokesperson Tommy Pigott said. A shaky truce between Israel and the Hezbollah militant group in Lebanon had been due to end on Sunday.

"We hope these discussions will advance lasting peace between the two countries, full recognition of each other's sovereignty and territorial integrity, and establishing genuine security along their shared border," Pigott said on social media.

While a key objective of Friday's talks was extending the tenuous ceasefire between Israel and Hezbollah, both sides continue to trade strikes.

The Israeli military said Friday it struck Hezbollah sites in southern Lebanon after reporting hostile aircraft alerts and launches from across the border.

Lebanon's health ministry said nearly 40 people were wounded in Israeli strikes near the coastal city of Tyre.

One strike "levelled" a primary health center and also damaged the neighbouring Hiram Hospital, wounding six medical staff members, the statement said.

payload.title: Israelin ja Libanonin tulitaukoa jatketaan 45 päivällä, Yhdysvallat kertoo
payload.summary: Yhdysvaltain ulkoministeriön mukaan Israel ja Libanon ovat sopineet 45 päivän jatkosta hauraalle tulitauolle Washingtonissa käytyjen neuvottelujen jälkeen. Samaan aikaan Israel teki iskuja Etelä-Libanonissa Tyren alueella.
payload.content:
Israel ja Libanon ovat sopineet 45 päivän jatkosta hauraalle tulitauolle, jonka oli määrä päättyä sunnuntaina, Yhdysvaltain ulkoministeriö kertoi perjantaina. Sopimus syntyi Washingtonissa käytyjen kaksipäiväisten neuvottelujen jälkeen, vaikka Israelin ja Hizbollahin välinen tilanne Etelä-Libanonissa pysyi samaan aikaan väkivaltaisena ja osapuolet jatkoivat iskujen vaihtoa.

## Neuvottelut jatkuvat kesäkuussa

Yhdysvaltain ulkoministeriön edustaja Tommy Pigott kuvasi Washingtonin keskusteluja tuottaviksi. Hänen mukaansa seuraavat neuvottelut on määrä pitää 2. ja 3. kesäkuuta. Pigott sanoi sosiaalisessa mediassa, että Yhdysvallat toivoo keskustelujen edistävän pysyvää rauhaa, maiden suvereniteetin ja alueellisen koskemattomuuden täyttä tunnustamista sekä todellista turvallisuutta Israelin ja Libanonin yhteisellä rajalla.

Tulitauon jatkaminen oli yksi perjantain neuvottelujen keskeisistä tavoitteista. Aselevon taustalla on Israelin ja Libanonissa toimivan Hizbollahin välinen konflikti. Lähdeaineiston mukaan Hizbollah on Iranin tukema shiiamuslimiliike, eikä se ole osa diplomaattisia tulitaukoneuvotteluja.

## Iskut jatkuivat Tyren alueella

Neuvottelujen päättyessä Israelin armeija antoi evakuointimääräyksiä Etelä-Libanonissa sijaitsevaan Tyren kaupunkiin. Armeijan mukaan se iski alueella Hizbollahin infrastruktuuriin. Paikan päällä olleen AFP:n toimittajan mukaan alueella kuultiin useita iskuja, joista kaksi tapahtui Tyren lähellä.

Libanonin valtiollisen median mukaan yksi iskuista kohdistui paikallisen järjestön ylläpitämään keskukseen sairaalan lähellä. Israelin armeija kertoi iskeneensä Hizbollahin kohteisiin Etelä-Libanonissa sen jälkeen, kun se oli raportoinut vihamielisistä ilma-aluksista ja rajan yli tehdyistä laukaisuista.

Libanonin terveysministeriön mukaan Tyren alueen iskuissa haavoittui ainakin 37 ihmistä. Haavoittuneiden joukossa oli kuusi sairaalan työntekijää, yhdeksän naista ja neljä lasta. Tulitauon jatkaminen antaa Washingtonin neuvotteluille lisää aikaa, mutta Tyren alueen tapahtumat osoittavat, että rajan turvallisuustilanne pysyy epävakaana myös diplomaattisen prosessin jatkuessa.
